analysis.title: Wall Street puked semis, now comes the chase
key_insights: SOX bounced hard and reclaimed its trendline. The note says one day does not make a bull market, but the positioning washout in semis was extreme.
If semis squeeze further, underweight investors would be forced to chase the move higher.
The five-day SOX performance through Thursday's close was the worst since Covid, per LSEG Workspace data.
Per GS, the positioning washout has pushed semiconductor allocations back toward year lows.
Per MS Alpha, SOX trades on a single-digit two-year forward P/E. The note compares this with the two-year forward P/E of consumer staples (GS chart).

BofA's Hartnett flagged on Friday that SOX traded 17% below its 200-day moving average. Readings of 20-25% below have historically offered attractive entry points since 1996. SOX has since rallied sharply.

sector_views.rationale: The note is constructive on a squeeze: positioning is washed out, allocations are near year lows and valuation is single-digit forward P/E. It cautions that one day is not a bull market.

risk_factors: One day's bounce does not confirm a trend reversal.
